gaps.sentence: They're building ___ new library near the town hall.
gaps.explanation: A new library — first mention; the town hall is the known one.

gaps.sentence: These apples cost two euros ___ kilo.
gaps.explanation: 'A/per' is used for rates: two euros a kilo, twice a week, 60 km an hour.

gaps.sentence: ___ Hyde Park is lovely in autumn.
gaps.explanation: Most park names take no article: Hyde Park, Central Park (exception: the Grands Boulevards style names).

gaps.sentence: Mount Everest is ___ highest mountain in the world.
___ United Kingdom consists of four countries.
gaps.explanation: 'The United Kingdom', 'the USA', 'the Czech Republic' all take 'the'.

gaps.sentence: ___ noise pollution in cities is getting worse.
gaps.explanation: 'Noise pollution' as a general concept takes no article.

gaps.sentence: We bought ___ antique mirror at the flea market.
gaps.explanation: 'An antique mirror' — 'antique' starts with a vowel sound.

gaps.sentence: His wife goes to ___ prison every Sunday to visit him.
gaps.explanation: Here 'the prison' is the building she visits, not the institution of imprisonment.
